name: Los Angeles
summary: A vast, sunny, car-shaped sprawl of distinct neighborhoods stretching from the mountains to the Pacific, home to Hollywood and the studios, beach towns, taco trucks, a growing Metro rail network and food from everywhere.

curated-2026-10.title: Los Angeles places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move fast here: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical 2025 asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Los Angeles (Downtown)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals for downtown Los Angeles; coastal areas run cooler in summer and inland valleys run hotter. Refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown LA
neighborhoods.summary: Skyscrapers, the Arts District, Little Tokyo, Grand Park and Olvera Street packed into a core that is finally walkable, with Metro lines converging at Union Station.

neighborhoods.name: Hollywood
neighborhoods.summary: Walk of Fame crowds, historic theaters, studios and music venues below the Hollywood Sign, with courtyard apartments climbing the hills.

neighborhoods.name: West Hollywood
neighborhoods.summary: A small, walkable city of Sunset Strip clubs, design showrooms, LGBTQ nightlife on Santa Monica Boulevard and Cedars-Sinai nearby.

neighborhoods.name: Beverly Hills
neighborhoods.summary: Rodeo Drive boutiques, palm-lined streets, grand hotels and mansions, plus talent agencies and medical offices.

neighborhoods.name: Mid-Wilshire and Miracle Mile

neighborhoods.name: Koreatown

neighborhoods.name: Silver Lake

neighborhoods.name: Echo Park

neighborhoods.name: Los Feliz

neighborhoods.name: Westwood

neighborhoods.name: Santa Monica

neighborhoods.name: Long Beach

transit.name: LA Metro Rail

transit.name: Catalina Express

local_color.name: May Gray and June Gloom
local_color.summary: Overcast coastal mornings in late spring and early summer that burn off by afternoon; locals complain but the beaches are empty.

local_color.name: Santa Ana winds
local_color.summary: Hot, dry offshore winds in fall that raise fire risk and set everyone on edge.

local_color.name: Car culture and valet parking
local_color.summary: Driving is the default, parking is a daily puzzle, and valet stands appear outside most restaurants.

local_color.name: Hiking culture
local_color.summary: Locals do sunrise hikes and sunset walks on canyon trails like Runyon and Griffith Park.

local_color.name: Neighborhood farmers' markets
local_color.summary: Nearly every neighborhood has a weekly market, treated as a social event.

local_color.name: "The Valley" and "the Westside"
local_color.summary: The San Fernando Valley is just 'the Valley'; the Westside means Santa Monica, Venice and nearby. People rarely cross town.

local_color.name: Los Angeles Dodgers
local_color.summary: Baseball's blue-and-white franchise at Dodger Stadium, with fans who leave in the seventh inning to beat traffic.

local_color.name: Los Angeles Angels
local_color.summary: The other baseball team, playing in Anaheim.

local_color.name: Los Angeles Lakers
local_color.summary: The purple-and-gold NBA franchise, a source of pride and celebrity courtside seats.

local_color.name: Los Angeles Clippers
local_color.summary: The NBA team that moved to the Intuit Dome in 2024.

local_color.name: Los Angeles Kings
local_color.summary: NHL hockey team in a city of surfers, playing at Crypto.com Arena.

local_color.name: Rams and Chargers
local_color.summary: Both of LA's NFL teams share SoFi Stadium in Inglewood.

local_color.name: LAFC and Angel City FC
local_color.summary: Two soccer clubs sharing BMO Stadium, known for loud supporters' groups.

local_color.name: Los Angeles Sparks
local_color.summary: WNBA team playing at Crypto.com Arena.
